title: What If One Number Was Too Big for Its Box? A Rocket Died

scenes.text: What if one number was too big for its box? In 1996 it destroyed a rocket.
Ariane 5 lifted off on June 4th, 1996, carrying four science satellites.
Thirty-seven seconds later, its guidance computer tried to squeeze a 64-bit number into 16 bits.
The number was too large, the software failed, and the error message was read as real flight data.
The engines swung hard over, the rocket broke apart, and it self-destructed about four kilometers up.
The code was reused from Ariane 4, which flew slower. The loss topped 370 million dollars.
